editorial:
Imagine you are living in a crowded house in the suburbs of Madrid, trying to make ends meet as an immigrant family. Everything feels a bit tight and stressful until the eldest sister comes home for a visit. She has joined a convent to become a nun, but it is pretty clear that she did not do it just for religion. She used the church as a way to get away from the pressures of her family and the expectations of society. The whole movie has a slow, cozy, but slightly tense feeling as you watch these siblings clash and reconnect.

What really makes this one work is the acting. You can feel the tension in the room without anyone even saying a word. While the story moves slowly, the emotional payoff is worth it. If you like old-school dramas that focus on family secrets and hidden feelings, you will love this. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a restored version. If you can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or rent it on Apple TV, go for it. Or, if you love physical media, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your collection is a great move for those crisp visuals.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a realization that the convent is not a magical cure for Angelina's problems. After spending time with her family, she understands that she was just running away from her life rather than moving toward a calling. She faces the truth about her desires and her family's flaws. The story ends with her making a choice about her future, leaving you to think about whether she truly finds peace or just a different kind of cage.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quiet family dramas and old Spanish cinema.
